## Overview and description

This project involves creating a database to manage peoples skills and roles. Throught this project you'll see displays of tables from the database a specific queries that display varying information regarding the tables below. 

## Crows-foot diagram

This is a diagram of 5 tables: SKILLS, PEOPLE, PEOPLE SKILLS, ROLES< PEOPLEROLES
Since the relationship between SKILLS -- PEOPLE and PEOPLE -- ROLES, is many-to-many, it was resolved with PEOPLESKILLS and PEOPLEROLES. This means that one skill and or role can appear multiple times but each entry in PEOPLESKILLS/PEOPLEROLES refers to only one skill and or role . One person can have multiple skills and roles through PEOPLESKILLS/PEOPLEROLES but each entry in PEOPLESKILLS/PEOPLEROLES refers to one person. 


```{mermaid}
erDiagram
SKILLS {
    int id PK
    string name
    string description
    string tag
    string url
    string time_commitment
   } 
    PEOPLESKILLS{
    int id PK
    int skills_id FK
    int people_id FK
    datetime date_acquired
   }

    PEOPLE{
    int id PK
    string first_name
    string last_name
    string email
    string linkedin_url
    string headshot_url
    string discord_handle
    string breif_bio
    datetime date_joined
   }

    ROLES{
       int id PK
       string name
       int sort_priority

    }

    PEOPLEROLES{
        int id PK
        int people_id FK
        int role_id FK
        string date_acquired
    }

    SKILLS ||--o| PEOPLESKILLS : contains
    PEOPLE ||--o| PEOPLESKILLS : has
    ROLES ||--o| PEOPLEROLES : contains
    PEOPLE ||--o| PEOPLEROLES : has
```

## Examples of data in the database

The following sections provide an overview of the schema including table names, and number of rows and columns in each table.

For the people, skills, and roles tables, a description of each table is presented along with it's contents.

### Tables and metrics in the database

```{python}
#| echo: false

# Get table names and column counts
col_df = run_sql_and_return_df(cnx,"""
    SELECT table_name as "table_name", COUNT(*) AS column_count
    FROM information_schema.columns
    WHERE table_schema = DATABASE()
    GROUP BY table_name;
""")

# Build dynamic row count queries using the table list
col_df['count_query'] = col_df['table_name'].apply(
    lambda name: f"SELECT '{name}' AS table_name, COUNT(*) AS row_count FROM `{name}`"
)

# Combine the queries into a single UNION ALL
full_query = "\nUNION ALL\n".join(col_df['count_query'].tolist())

# Execute the UNION ALL query to get row counts
row_df = run_sql_and_return_df(cnx,full_query)

import pandas as pd

# Merge with column counts
summary_df = pd.merge(row_df, col_df[['table_name', 'column_count']], on='table_name')

summary_df

```

### People table

The *people* table contains elements that describe  the individual people involved in this database system. It has their first and last name, email and linkedin profile with a headshot included, a bio and discord handle, and finally the date that they joined.

Below is a list of data in the *people* table.

```{python}
run_sql_and_return_html( cnx,f"""
select * from people;
""" )
```

### Skills table

The *skills* table contains elements that describe  the type of skills that people can acquire in the databse. It has the skills id, name a description of the skill, a tag, a url, and how much time commitment does this skill has (light, moderate, heavy).

Below is a list of data in the *skills* table.


```{python}
run_sql_and_return_html( cnx,f"""
select * from skills;
""" )
```

### Roles table

The *roles* table contains elements that describe the different types of roles that people can have within the work environment theres: Designer, Developer, Boss, Mentor, etc..

Below is a list of data in the *roles* table.


```{python}
run_sql_and_return_html( cnx,f"""
select * from roles;
""" )
```

## Sample queries

### List skill names of Person 5

```{python}
run_sql_and_return_html( cnx,f"""
select s.name
from skills s 
inner join peopleskills ps on s.id = ps.skills_id
where ps.people_id = 5;
""" )
```

### List people with Skill 2

```{python}
run_sql_and_return_html( cnx,f"""
select p.people_first_name, p.people_last_name 
from people p
inner join peopleskills ps on p.people_id = ps.people_id
INNER JOIN skills s ON ps.skills_id = s.id
WHERE s.id = 2;

""" )
```

### List people with a DEVELOPER role

```{python}
run_sql_and_return_html( cnx,f"""
select people.people_first_name, people.people_last_name
from peopleroles
join roles on peopleroles.role_id = roles.role_id
join people on peopleroles.people_id = people.people_id
where roles.role_name = 'Developer';
""" )
```

### List names and email addresses of people without skills

```{python}
run_sql_and_return_html( cnx,f"""
select p.people_first_name, p.people_last_name, p.people_email
FROM people p
LEFT JOIN peopleskills ps ON p.people_id = ps.people_id
WHERE ps.people_id IS NULL;
""" )
```

### List names and tags of unused skills

```{python}
run_sql_and_return_html( cnx,f"""
select s.name, s.tag
from skills s
left join peopleskills ps on s.id = ps.skills_id
where ps.skills_id IS NULL;
""" )
```

### List people names and skill names with the BOSS role

```{python}
run_sql_and_return_html( cnx,f"""
select p.people_first_name, p.people_last_name, s.name AS skill_name
from people p
join peopleroles pr on p.people_id = pr.people_id
join roles r on pr.role_id = r.role_id
join peopleskills ps on p.people_id = ps.people_id
join skills s on ps.skills_id = s.id
where r.role_name = 'Boss';
""" )
```

### List ids and names of unused roles

```{python}
run_sql_and_return_html( cnx,f"""
select r.role_id, r.role_name
from roles r
left join peopleroles pr on r.role_id = pr.role_id
where pr.role_id IS NULL;
""" )
```

### List people and the number of skills they have acquired.

(Goal: Practice JOIN, GROUP BY, and COUNT())

```{python}
run_sql_and_return_html( cnx,f"""
select p.people_first_name, p.people_last_name, COUNT(ps.skills_id) as skill_count
from people p
left join peopleskills ps on p.people_id = ps.people_id
group by p.people_id;
""" )
```

### List each skill and the number of people who have acquired it.

(Goal: Practice JOIN, GROUP BY, COUNT())

```{python}
run_sql_and_return_html( cnx,f"""
select s.name as skill_name, COUNT(ps.people_id) AS people_count
from skills s
left join peopleskills ps on s.id = ps.skills_id
group by s.id, s.name;
""" )
```

### List all people who have acquired more than 2 skills

(Goal: Join through multiple tables and use HAVING)


```{python}
run_sql_and_return_html( cnx,f"""
select p.people_first_name, p.people_last_name, COUNT(ps.skills_id) AS skill_count
from people p
join peopleskills ps on p.people_id = ps.people_id
group by p.people_id
HAVING COUNT(ps.skills_id) > 2;
""" )
```
